Plot each unit's sequence of assigned profiles across the occasions as a row of coloured cells

Source: R/plot-named.R
plot_sequences.Rd

plot_sequences() plots each group's (person's) sequence of profiles as a row of coloured cells: one row per group, one cell per occasion, coloured by the profile the observation at that occasion is assigned to (its most likely one). Within a block the rows are sorted by each group's most frequent profile, so groups with similar sequences sit together. An occasion at which nothing was observed is shown grey, and one absent from the data is left blank.

Usage

plot_sequences(
  x,
  labels = TRUE,
  cell_labels = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A fit with ordered occasions:

  • a transition fit from lta(), of either class (multilpa_transitions or multilpa_lta), except one with measurement = "occasion", whose profiles differ by occasion;

  • a profile or class fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() (with or without membership covariates) made with time.

labels

TRUE (default) puts the rows in blocks under labelled strips: one block per group class when the fit has two or more group classes, otherwise one per most frequent profile. FALSE draws the rows in the same order as one block without strips.

cell_labels

TRUE (default) prints the profile number in each cell when the grid has at most 60 rows and 40 occasions; a larger grid shows the profiles by colour, with a dash still marking an occasion that observed nothing when the grid also has noise or absent occasions. FALSE never prints the numbers.

main, subtitle

Title and subtitle of the plot, each one string; NULL (default) keeps the view's own.

Value

A ggplot object, which draws the plot when printed. Conditions raised:

  • latents_no_time: a profile or class fit made without time;

  • latents_nothing_to_plot: a model with no sequence view (an lta() fit with measurement = "occasion", a growth mixture, a mixture regression, an additive or cross-level fit, pooled imputations);

  • latents_not_a_fit: x is not a fitted model.

See also

plot_transitions() for the transition matrix. The sequences as a table: get_results(x, "sequences") for a profile or class model and a transition fit of class multilpa_transitions; get_results(x, "assignments") (one row per observation, with its profile) for a general transition fit of class multilpa_lta.

Examples

fit <- lta(course_engagement, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),
           id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence",
           n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
plot_sequences(fit)
